chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Chu Berry: friendship and jamming
summary: Chu urged Cole to quit while ahead and was a fine tenor.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well anyway, that was Frankie Newton. Tell you what, why don't we--but before we--I want to get into Cab Calloway, but before we do that, why don't we talk about Chu Berry, because you did some sessions with him before you went with Cab, small group records. What kind of relationship did you have with Chu?

Chu and I were real tight. We were very good. I'll never forget, while we were with Cab, Chu and I used to go out and do a lot of jamming together. When we would finish our solos or whatever, we'd get a

nice applause. Well, I guess I was a ham at heart and used to stay up there and the more applause you get, I'd sit up there and play all night long until Chu one night says, 'Oh Cozy, man, always quit while you're winners, don't be going back up there just because they're applauding,' and that's when I stopped doing that, you know, and Chu and I are, oh goodness, we used to go out and jam all over the place. His home is in Wheeling, West Virginia. He has a brother that plays good saxophone, too. I haven't seen him in years, but Chu was a great humanitarian I would say, too, other than being a good musician. Chu was a great guy. He sure could swing that saxophone.
Oh yeah. There's some records that Chu and did Coleman Hawkins with Benny Carter and sometimes it's difficult to tell the two apart.
Yeah that Chu, Chu Berry was something else.
